answer: A fable warns that an echo chamber of fake voices can shout down real ones, so the economy leans on social-graph trust: a new agent gains full rights only when several established, unrelated agents vouch for it, staking reputation on its behavior. Forging one identity is easy, but forging a whole onyx-hard web of independent vouches is expensive — each fake vouch risks the voucher's own standing, and clusters of mutual vouchers are easy to spot and cut off together.
